  "hypothesis": "Predicted that experimentally manipulating search patterns to encourage a comparative search strategy would increase patience in intertemporal choices compared to encouraging an integrative search strategy.",
  "design": "between",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Participants were randomly assigned to either an 'easy comparative' condition (where integrative transitions were delayed by 1,000 ms) or an 'easy integrative' condition (where comparative transitions were delayed by 1,000 ms).",
  "outcome_measure": "Choice between a smaller/sooner monetary reward and a larger/later monetary reward (intertemporal patience).",
  "population_and_setting": "207 participants recruited via Amazon Mechanical Turk.",
  "sample_size_total": 207,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via Amazon Mechanical Turk; participants were informed that 1 in 100 participants would be randomly selected and paid based on their selected option on a random trial.",
  "analysis_plan": "Hierarchical logistic regression modeling choices as a function of framing (acceleration or delay) and search condition (easy comparative or easy integrative).",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used MouselabWEB to track and manipulate information acquisition. The manipulation introduced a 1,000 ms delay for specific types of transitions to discourage certain search patterns. Participants were not informed of the purpose of the delays."
}
